playbook.title: Move after you get a kill
playbook.principle: A kill gives away your position: a red dot if you are unsuppressed, plus a killcam for the player you killed. The next enemy comes to that spot.
good: Stepping back or shifting a few metres after the kill
Reloading behind cover
Pre-aiming where the next enemy will swing from
bad: Staying on the same angle and dying to the teammate of the player you killed
signals: Dying a few seconds after your own kill, at the same spot
playbook.fix: After every kill, move, reload in cover, then aim at the next likely entrance.

playbook.title: Play within trading distance
playbook.principle: Stay close enough that a teammate can kill your killer straight away, but far enough apart that one spray or grenade does not get you both.
good: A teammate covering your angle a few seconds behind
Trading kills
Never the lone player on a flank
bad: Far from every friendly dot
Stacked on a teammate and both killed together
signals: Death screen: no friendly dots near you on the minimap
playbook.fix: Stay one short sprint from a teammate who covers a different angle.

playbook.title: Do not sprint into likely contact
playbook.principle: After sprinting there is a delay before you can fire, longer after tactical sprint. A pre-aimed enemy wins that window, so slow down near corners and doorways with your gun up.
good: Releasing sprint before corners and doorways
Entering with the gun already up
bad: Rounding corners at full tactical sprint
Dying before the gun comes up
signals: Killcam: your gun lowered in a sprint pose when the first shot lands
playbook.fix: Stop sprinting before any corner or doorway that could hold an enemy.

sources.title: MW4 day-one habits, Techyorker
Sprinting vs ADS timing, MitchCactus

playbook.title: Reload behind cover, not in the open
playbook.principle: A magazine usually holds more than one kill, so reloading after every burst wastes your safest moments. Reload when you are out of sight.
good: Checking ammo, stepping behind cover, then reloading
Switching to the sidearm if caught empty
bad: Reloading in the open right after a kill
A reload interrupted by the next enemy
signals: Killcam or HUD: reload animation or an empty magazine at the moment of death
playbook.fix: Reload only behind cover, or finish the fight with your pistol.

Gunfight tips, TechRadar

playbook.title: Pre-aim common angles at head height
playbook.principle: Keep your crosshair where enemies will appear, at head height, so a fight needs only a small correction. Scump teaches this as centering.
good: Crosshair leading around corners at head height
Clearing one angle at a time
bad: Crosshair on the floor or a wall when you round a corner
Late flicks
signals: Killcam: you aimed away from where the killer appeared and turned only after being hit
playbook.fix: Before every corner, put your crosshair at head height where the enemy would appear.

playbook.drill: Private match: walk each map pre-aiming every doorway.

playbook.title: Peek cheaply for information
playbook.principle: When you do not know if an angle is held, use a short jiggle, a mantle you can abort, or a quick slide peek before you commit. MW4 lets you steer and abort mantles.
good: A quick jiggle, then a committed swing
Aborting a mantle when you see an enemy
Utility before the peek
bad: A slow, wide peek into a held angle
Committing to a full mantle in the open
signals: Killcam: you died mid-mantle or during a slow, wide strafe into a lane
playbook.fix: Jiggle or abort the mantle to get information, then commit once you know.

playbook.title: Read the minimap every few seconds
playbook.principle: In MW4, red dots show when an enemy fires an unsuppressed weapon or your UAV is up. Firing unsuppressed puts you on their minimap too.
good: Glancing at the map every few seconds
Moving toward red dots from an unexpected angle
A suppressor when you want to stay hidden
bad: Dying to an enemy who showed as a dot seconds earlier
Firing unsuppressed from one spot and getting flanked
signals: Death screen: a red dot near the killer before you died
playbook.fix: Check the minimap before every corner and face red dots before they reach you.

playbook.title: Play around UAVs
playbook.principle: With your UAV up, push with the information. With theirs up, assume you are seen unless you run Ghost, so stay near teammates and cover.
good: Pushing the moment your UAV goes up
Playing near teammates under an enemy UAV
Shooting it down
bad: Holding a lonely flank under an enemy UAV without Ghost
signals: An enemy UAV shortly before death, killer from behind or the side
playbook.fix: Under an enemy UAV, stay near teammates and cover or run Ghost; under yours, push.

playbook.title: Know where they will spawn
playbook.principle: Spawns depend on where both teams are. Pushing too deep, spreading out or wiping the enemy can flip spawns behind you.
good: Knowing the current enemy spawn
Holding angles that face it
Expecting a flip after a big push
bad: Chasing deep into their side
Getting shot in the back by freshly spawned enemies
signals: Killcam: the killer behind you, on the side your team held, early in their life
playbook.fix: After a wipe or a deep push, turn around, regroup and expect the spawns to flip.

playbook.title: Take power positions as a team
playbook.principle: Rambo: Call of Duty is a game of positional warfare. Positions that see the most lanes and the enemy spawn exits create favourable fights.
good: Overlapping lanes toward the enemy spawn
A power spot held with a teammate
bad: Alone in a power spot with no trade
Leaving a power spot to chase kills
signals: Killcam: crossfire from two directions on a spot your team held
playbook.fix: Learn two or three power positions per map and take them with a teammate.

playbook.title: Fight at your weapon's range
playbook.principle: SMGs and shotguns win close, assault rifles win mid range, snipers and marksman rifles win long. Damage drops with distance, so fights outside your range are uphill.

Assault rifle holding mid lanes

A long gun in a cramped room against a shotgun

playbook.title: Shoot first, be ready first
playbook.principle: Whoever lands the first shot usually wins. Arriving pre-aimed, gun up and not sprinting decides most duels.

Pre-aimed and firing on sight
bad: Reacting to being shot
Taking damage before your first shot

playbook.title: Hipfire close, aim at range, strafe

Aiming before peeking a mid lane
Strafing while firing
bad: Aiming down sights at point blank and losing the race
Standing still while aimed in a long lane
signals: Killcam: you scoped in at point blank, or stood still while the killer strafed

bad: Re-peeking at low health

strengths: Punish players camping roofs or upper floors
Clear an indoor Hardpoint/flag

Break a team holding a Hardpoint
counters: Destroy the beacon
Move away from it immediately
Cold-Blooded may help vs targeting (unconfirmed)

Clear a long lane full of enemies

Leave the marked line

counters: Shoot it down with launchers or a SAM turret
Rely on audio and callouts while jammed

arsenal.name: Combat Drone

strengths: Clear rooms and objective buildings
Hunt campers in corners
counters: Shoot it down
DDOS or Shock Stick
Cold-Blooded may help vs targeting (unconfirmed)
tips: Use your own team as cover while piloting; your body is exposed
arsenal.look: User: drone camera view with reticle. Victims: small drone flying through rooms, audible buzzing.

strengths: Hold an objective or lane hands-free
Guard your flank while you anchor
counters: Launchers (RPG-8/JOKR)
Shock Stick
DDOS
Cold-Blooded vs AI targeting
tips: Deploy near the objective so it fights on your terms

counters: Stay under cover and move between buildings
Cold-Blooded (unconfirmed)
tips: Lock enemies standing on flags/hills first
arsenal.look: User: aerial targeting view with lock-on boxes. Victims: missiles falling from above.

arsenal.name: Railgun Sentry

strengths: Lock down a lane, doorway or Hardpoint entrance
counters: Cold-Blooded vs AI targeting
Approach from behind/outside its view
Launchers
Drill Charge
tips: Place it covering the angle you can't watch, not the one you already hold
arsenal.look: A tripod railgun turret; high-velocity bright tracer shots; killfeed shows a sentry icon.

arsenal.name: Attack Helicopter
arsenal.summary: AI helicopter that patrols the map and engages enemies on its own.
strengths: Late-game lockdown when enemies fight outdoors
counters: PILA (guided), JOKR (lock-on top attack), SAM Airburst Turret
Cold-Blooded
Stay indoors
tips: Call it while you hold power positions; it covers outdoor lanes
arsenal.look: A helicopter circles overhead firing at players; tracer fire and rotor sound; killfeed helicopter icon.

arsenal.name: Advanced UAV

strengths: Full-map intel for the whole team during a push
Objective modes late game
counters: Counter UAV
DDOS-type jamming
Play indoors and keep moving
Ghost vs Advanced UAV unconfirmed in MW4

counters: Launchers and SAM turret

tips: Burst-fire to manage turret heat
arsenal.look: User: helicopter gunner view with twin turret reticles and a heat meter. Victims: helicopter hovering and firing in bursts.

arsenal.name: Argonaut

counters: Focus fire as a team
Launchers and explosives
Keep distance from the cluster launcher
tips: Move with teammates; you are slow and a magnet for focus fire
arsenal.look: User: first-person armored suit visuals with a grenade launcher. Victims: a bulky armored operator; cluster-grenade explosions.

arsenal.name: Gunship

counters: Launchers

Cold-Blooded vs thermal
Stay under hard cover
tips: Use the 105 mm on objectives, 25 mm on runners
arsenal.look: User: thermal top-down view with cannon reticles. Victims: heavy cannon impacts and a gunship circling.

arsenal.name: Air Lockdown

counters: Kill the player on a long streak; focus them as a team

Staying pinned in spawn instead of using flanks when spawns don't flip

limitations: Frames are sampled every 2–3 seconds, so fast deaths and kills can be missed; deaths are mostly caught on the killcam or death screen.
Death areas need a visible, fixed minimap; they are approximate.
Map, weapon and perk lists come from launch-week research; check them after patches.
Live tips only in the campaign and private matches with bots; everything online is reviewed after the match.

Fight details (cover, movement, range, height, support) are read from the killcam, which is a reconstruction and can be slightly off; findings are probable, not certain, and untagged deaths are counted, never guessed.
Kills are tagged only with what the player's own view shows (range, movement, height).
